newsitem.title: GERMANY: Neo-Nazis rampage through north German town.
newsitem.headline: Neo-Nazis rampage through north German town.

text.p: Hundreds of German neo-Nazis and dozens of left-wing extremists smashed windows and rampaged through the northern town of Muenden on Thursday after police broke up an illegal right-wing rally here.

Police said they had arrested several people in Muenden, where the right-wing National Democratic Party of Germany (NPD) organised an impromptu rally after authorities banned a march in Leipzig coinciding with May Day demonstrations there.
Around 150 left-wing extremists in Leipzig hurled rocks and fireworks at police, who were trying to keep them apart from a small group of skinheads defying the ban of the NPD rally.
Leipzig police said they had stopped around 140 right-wing and left-wing extremists from entering the city.

Thousands of police were on duty in Leipzig and Berlin bracing for such violence as demonstrators gathered for mass Labour day rallies across the country which have often ended in clashes with police.
Left-wing extremists in Berlin have targeted expensive cars, shops and bars in the past. They went on the rampage 10 years ago on May 1, setting fire to a supermarket.
Union members were expected to form a human chain around the centre of Leipzig to symbolise protecting the town from rising right-wing extremism.
